place_01.title: Kożuchów Castle
place_01.shortDescription: 13th-14th century fortress built by the Piast Dukes of Głogów and Żagań.
place_01.fullDescription: Kożuchów Castle is a medieval fortress erected in the 13th-14th centuries on the site of an earlier timber-and-earth stronghold. Built on stilts in marshy terrain, it conceals a 14th-century cylindrical bergfried (keep) with starvation dungeons completely enclosed inside later wings. Prince Sigismund Jagiellon (later King Sigismund I the Old) resided here. The castle survived the great city fire of 1488 and stands today as the military heart of the region.
place_01.funFact: The 14th-century cylindrical defense tower with 2.6-meter-thick stone walls is completely enclosed inside the castle building and cannot be seen from the outside!

place_02.title: Church of Our Lady of the Candlemas
place_02.shortDescription: Monumental 13th-century church with a stone head and ships on the ceiling.
place_02.fullDescription: The Church of Our Lady of Candlemas (formerly St. John the Baptist) is the oldest sacred building in Kożuchów, originally built in the 13th century from Romanesque cut stone blocks and later expanded in Gothic and Baroque styles. A mysterious early medieval sculpture known as the 'Head in the Wall' is embedded in the chancel wall. The Baroque vault features stucco nautical sailing ships—an extraordinary motif for an inland church.
place_02.funFact: This inland church in Western Poland features an elaborate fleet of ocean-going sailing ships carved in relief on the ceiling!

place_03.title: Krosno Gate Tower
place_03.shortDescription: 14th-century medieval gate tower rising over 20 meters high.
place_03.fullDescription: The Krosno Gate Tower is the sole surviving part of the three fortified gate complexes that once guarded Kożuchów. Built in the 14th century along the stone defensive walls, it stands over 20 meters high with original keyhole and slit embrasures. It was spared from demolition in the 19th century because it was converted into apartments, and today it houses regional museum exhibits.
place_03.funFact: The tower was spared demolition in the 19th century solely because it was converted into municipal apartments for impoverished townsfolk!

place_04.title: Medieval Defensive Walls & Moat
place_04.shortDescription: One of the most complete surviving medieval city wall circuits in Europe.
place_04.fullDescription: The medieval town walls of Kożuchów form an almost complete ring of stone-and-brick fortifications from the turn of the 13th and 14th centuries, with a perimeter exceeding 1,000 meters and heights up to 8 meters. Originally reinforced with dozens of open-backed bastions, the dry moat up to 20 meters wide was transformed into a serene green promenade in the 19th century.
place_04.funFact: Over 90% of the medieval defensive ring remains intact, making it one of the best-preserved medieval circuits in all of Central Europe!

place_05.title: Bastion - "Executioner's House"
place_05.shortDescription: Medieval watchtower bastion adapted as the town executioner's dwelling.
place_05.fullDescription: This bastion, known as the Executioner's House, is a former medieval watchtower built into the southwestern ramparts. Due to the infamous and ostracized nature of his trade, the municipal executioner was forced to reside away from the community on the outer periphery of the walls.
place_05.funFact: In medieval and early modern times, executioners also performed municipal cleansing and were licensed to set broken bones!

place_06.title: Town Hall & Market Square
place_06.shortDescription: Historic square with a Gothic-Neoclassical Town Hall and ancient cellars.
place_06.fullDescription: Kożuchów's Market Square was laid out in the 13th century on a regular chessboard grid. At its center stands the Town Hall with Gothic origins, remodeled in Renaissance and Neoclassical styles. Deep multi-level cellars extend beneath the square, where Kożuchów's celebrated beer was once aged.
place_06.funFact: In the 15th century, beer brewed in Kożuchów was so renowned that it was exported directly to the ducal courts in Głogów and Wrocław!

place_07.title: Lapidarium of Sepulchral Art
place_07.shortDescription: Historic 17th-century cemetery with nearly 200 tombstones and epitaphs.
place_07.fullDescription: The Lapidarium of Sepulchral Art on 1 Maja Street is a unique 17th-century Protestant burial ground founded in 1634. Nearly 200 Renaissance, Baroque, and Rococo gravestones and epitaphs are embedded in the cemetery wall and chapel structures, presenting rich vanitas symbolism (hourglasses, skulls, Chronos).
place_07.funFact: It is widely recognized as one of the best-preserved and richest Protestant sepulchral lapidaria in Central Europe!

place_08.title: Baroque Portico & City Park
place_08.shortDescription: 1780 palace portico adorned with herm statues and monumental trees.
place_08.fullDescription: The Baroque pillared portico in the City Park is the surviving remnant of the von Kalckreuth family residence erected in 1780 (the palace was destroyed in 1945). The four pillars are crowned by sculpted stone herms. The surrounding park contains a monument to Enlightenment philosopher Salomon Maimon and centuries-old plane trees.
place_08.funFact: Salomon Maimon, buried in Kożuchów, was praised by Immanuel Kant as one of the sharpest critics and deepest thinkers of his philosophy!

place_09.title: Historic Facade on Klasztorna Street
place_09.shortDescription: Surviving 18th-century facade adorned with bas-reliefs of St. Peter and St. Paul.
place_09.fullDescription: The historic facade on Klasztorna Street is the preserved 18th-century front wall of a townhouse, retained as a monument after the demolished building was cleared in 1959. It features ornate stucco reliefs depicting St. Peter with keys and St. Paul with a sword.
place_09.funFact: The facade stands completely freestanding like a theatrical stage set—a green park square lies directly behind it!

place_10.title: Church of the Holy Spirit
place_10.shortDescription: Medieval hospital church from the turn of the 13th and 14th centuries.
place_10.fullDescription: The Church of the Holy Spirit is a 14th-century Gothic hospital church founded to serve an almshouse outside the city walls. It represents the only preserved trace of medieval healthcare in the region, featuring late Gothic net vaulting and a gabled facade.
place_10.funFact: In medieval times, hospitals were not medical clinics but hospices and shelters for the sick, poor, and arriving pilgrims!
place_10.openingHours: Open during religious services and on request

place_11.title: Evangelical Church Tower
place_11.shortDescription: Monumental tower from 1826, relic of a historic Church of Grace.
place_11.fullDescription: The tower on Evangelical Square is a monumental remnant of one of Silesia's six historic Churches of Grace permitted under the Treaty of Altranstädt in 1709. While the timber-framed church was dismantled in the 1960s, the majestic 1826 neoclassical tower still commands the skyline.
place_11.funFact: This Church of Grace was one of only six Protestant churches permitted by the Austrian Emperor across all of Silesia!

place_12.title: Historic Water Tower
place_12.shortDescription: 39-meter municipal engineering monument from 1908 in Neo-Gothic style.
place_12.fullDescription: Kożuchów's historic water tower from 1908 is a municipal engineering marvel built on the town's highest summit (112 m above sea level). Constructed from red clinker brick in Neo-Gothic and Art Nouveau style, it houses a steel Intze reservoir with a 150 m³ capacity.
place_12.funFact: Because it was built on the town's highest hill, municipal water pressure was maintained entirely by natural gravity without electric pumps!
